capabilities: Convert single or batch lecture PDFs into structured Markdown notes with headings, formulas and a progress HUD
OCR pasted screenshots, slides and whiteboard photos into Markdown with LaTeX and diagrams
Chat with configured LLM providers in a sidebar, attaching vault notes with @ and streaming Markdown, math and Mermaid replies
Build a local embedding index over a course folder and retrieve relevant chunks with [[Note#Section]] citations during chat
Manage multiple LLM API profiles and per-vault chat sessions
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README includes detailed security and privacy notes (local-first storage, encrypted API keys, no telemetry, a table of network destinations) plus automated-review notes; first use of PDF/embedding features may download runtime files (ONNX, PDF.js) and embedding model weights over the network. Community links: changelog, docs, and GitHub releases.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to turn course PDFs and slide images into structured notes or to query your own course materials with an LLM, so students must juggle external conversion and chat tools.
